storage.recommended_seam: A user-defined storage adapter behind each vendor's storage seam (Cognito: a KeyValueStorageInterface implementation; Auth0: a custom ICache) so a storage change becomes a one-file swap. The bounded fixtures demonstrate both.

cost_evidence.basis: Both surfaces localize the change to a single file each: the Cognito selector line sits inside the adapter, and the Auth0 config lives in one helper. No call sites elsewhere depend on storage shape.

cognito.note: Owned 401 → refresh → retry → failure path exists; no single-flight deduplication.

refresh.recommended_seam: Add a single-flight helper on the Cognito path and route onRefresh through it; bring the Auth0 surface behind the same AuthPort so the API client's 401 path covers it.

cost_evidence.basis: Cognito side: one small helper file (single-flight) — the ownership shape already exists. Auth0 side: no 401 path exists at all; owning refresh there means porting the surface behind the port first (two app files).

cognito.note: A Cognito → other-provider swap on this side is a new sibling adapter.

identity_provider.recommended_seam: Bring the Auth0 surface behind the existing AuthPort (a second adapter implementing the same port) — two files to migrate; the Cognito side is already in place.

cost_evidence.basis: Auth0-specific surface used directly in two app-layer files with no seam localizing it; the Cognito side is confined to one adapter, so the port to implement against already exists.

cognito.note: Domain-Principal-ready; the policy gap is not load-bearing yet.

auth0.note: Inline namespaced-claim reads, hard-coded roles, and the audience-less opaque-token anti-pattern.

authorization.recommended_seam: Configure audience on the Auth0 client and request it on token calls; route claim/role decisions through the AuthPort + domain Principal + a policy layer (the same policy module the Cognito side needs before authz decisions reach app code).

cost_evidence.basis: Auth0 side: inline reads and hard-coded roles in one component plus the audience fix in one helper. Cognito side: policy module still to be written, but claim mapping is already localized to the adapter.

judgment_calls.question: Is a token storage change actually on the table (HttpOnly cookies, encrypted store, session cookies)? On the Cognito side the current storage LOOKS custom but is a built-in selector — acceptable for now, or on the critical path of a cookie move?
Is fully owning refresh (single-flight + explicit failure path, on both surfaces) on the roadmap, independent of the migration?
What is driving the Auth0 → Cognito migration (cost, compliance, consolidation) and what is the timeline?
judgment_calls.context: Completion makes the Auth0-side findings about-to-be-deleted; indefinite coexistence makes them load-bearing for years. Cannot be inferred from code.

judgment_calls.question: Are authorization model changes planned (RBAC/finer permissions)? And is the opaque-token anti-pattern breaking something today — does the backend reject these tokens (current bug) or accept them informally (latent risk)?
Is Firebase on the auth path anywhere in the broader codebase? The imports observed here are analytics-only, but the skill cannot verify that without a firebase profile.
judgment_calls.context: If Firebase Auth appears elsewhere, this audit is incomplete and a firebase profile should be added before the next run.

judgment_calls.question: True retrofit cost: all cost evidence is qualitative — real time-to-complete depends on team bandwidth and how much of the Auth0 surface lives outside this fixture's analyzed scope.

headline.text: The Auth0 side trips a provider-specific anti-pattern: createAuth0Client is configured with no audience and getTokenSilently is called without one — per Auth0's docs the returned token is opaque (non-JWT), not a valid API access token. Worth surfacing now, before the migration locks in around it.
